headline: IML's Marc Whittaker sees Reliance Worldwide as a cheap, best-in-class plumbing fittings business poised to rebound after 20%+ underperformance
reasoning: Reliance Worldwide trades on 12x earnings and has underperformed the ASX 300 by at least 20% over the past 12 months. A large portion of revenues are non-discretionary repair and renovation work, providing earnings resilience. Management has already confirmed guidance, reducing downside surprise risk. Any positive outlook commentary at results could be a meaningful catalyst for a re-rating given how cheaply the stock is valued.
quote: It's trading on 12 times. It's best in class and what it does. So think about behind the wall plumbing fittings. Push to connect to for plumbing piping bathrooms, kitchens and so forth. They're moving from a brass based product to a stainless steel based product. A big issue for them has been the volatility in the copper price, and the fact they haven't been able to plan forward with enough sort of confidence and visibility, given the volatility in copper. So they're moving away from that to a stainless steel product, which gives you the same outcome, same quality of product. Plumbers like it particularly in the US. I like that recurring non-discretionary element to their revenues. It has confirmed guidance already. So keep that in mind. So we shouldn't be surprised on the downside. headline: Marc Whittaker backs Hanson Technologies as mission-critical billing software trading at a significant discount after underperforming by 30%
reasoning: Hanson Technologies provides mission-critical billing and customer management software to water utilities, electricity utilities, and telcos — industries where switching providers is practically impossible due to complexity and regulation. Despite the de-rating, the business is fundamentally strong: first-half recurring revenue grew ~16% and cash EBITDA margins are around 70%. Whittaker contrasts it favourably with 'nice to have' software, categorising Hanson as a 'must have' with strong incumbency advantages, making the current price attractively cheap.
quote: Hanson falls into that former category. Absolutely. Mission critical. You must have them. They operate in very complex, highly regulated industries. So, you know, electricity, water, telcos. You can't just switch and mix providers. Once you're in there the inertia and incumbency advantages are very strong. So again trading on 14 times earnings so degraded quite a bit. It's underperformed the market by about 30% or over 30% over the last 12 months. A very good company generates good cash. Have them confirmed guidance but they don't need to if they haven't come to the market and there's not any change. Their first half result was very strong recurring revenue growth of about 16%. So cash EBITDA margins of about 70%. So very strong very strong business a lot to like about it. Very resilient, very enduring, as I say, mission critical and attractively priced as well.
